quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Using the front and rear brakes at the same time:

options.text: Gives you the most stopping power.
Should not be done at highway speeds.
Does not work well for stopping a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you the most stopping power.
questions.explanation: The best way to stop in a straight line is to use both the front and rear brakes fully at the same time, without locking either wheel.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It will only take a few minutes.

questions.question: A helmet is:

options.text: Required only for new riders with a license less than two years old.
Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.
questions.explanation: In Alabama, all motorcycle riders and passengers must wear an approved helmet. Helmets protect your head and neck in an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of strong material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver did not yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by car drivers not yielding to motorcycles. Never assume that car drivers will yield, even if they are supposed to.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space and slow down. Be ready to stop when approaching an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a green signal that lets you turn.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol faster, it builds up in your system. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward. They can get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at flashing railroad crossing lights. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles is at intersections.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What separates traffic lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How can you best help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlight and running lights to help others see you. Use your high beam both day and night when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding to make yourself more noticeable, even during the day.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles is at intersections. Oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcycles are the biggest danger.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow.

questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is oily but usually offers enough traction for safe riding, unless it rains. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to support your body weight.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a way that lets your arms control the motorcycle. Do not position yourself so your arms must hold up your body weight.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following factors may affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The three main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle can:

options.text: Put you in the vehicle's blind spot.
Help the other driver see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot. If they cannot see you, they may change lanes and hit you. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them one at a time. Do not brake while swerving. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide. You can often ride to the left or right of it and still be in the center of the lane.
